result.title: An Educated Guess: Deriving Statistically Aligned Gradient Estimates for Zeroth-Order Optimisation
result.summary: As novel hardware architectures are explored for the purposes of machine learning, including neuromorphic chips, asynchronous systems, and ASICs, effective learning algorithms are highly desirable. While backpropagation is the standard for differentiation on standard hardware, its requirement for global synchrony and exact differentiability limits the exploration of exotic algorithms on non-traditional substrates and devices. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation methods, such as SPSA and weight perturbation, offer a compelling alternative by estimating gradients through inference-only passes; however, these methods have historically suffered due to the `curse of dimensionality', where random perturbations become increasingly misaligned with the true gradient in high-dimensional spaces. In this work, we move beyond blind random noise by deriving zeroth-order search directions from activation geometry available during the forward pass. This leads to a family of Spectral Zeroth-Order methods, SZO-$κ$, whose directions solve local response-based gradient-guessing objectives under explicit stochastic assumptions. These methods explore feature-supported directions that are more likely to produce informative loss responses. Using multilayer and convolutional networks, we analyse gradient alignment, bias-variance structure, and training stability of these methods relative to standard perturbation baselines and backpropagation.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Spectral Zeroth-Order 方法族 SZO-κ，用前向传播中可得的激活几何构造零阶优化的搜索方向，替代盲随机扰动，并在多层与卷积网络上分析其梯度对齐、偏差-方差结构和训练稳定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用内部激活几何引导梯度估计」的思路，可能为 latent 推理多步轨迹中的贡献分配与免反传训练监督提供线索，值得核查该方向构造能否用于 latent 状态的更新信号，但原文并不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
